method.name: Welch's independent-samples t-test
method.evaluates: Whether the mean of the measurement differs between the two groups.
method.null_hypothesis: The two groups have equal population means.
assumptions: Each row is treated as an independent observation. Paired or repeated measurements of the same subject are not supported.

Each group's mean is approximately normally distributed: the values are roughly normal, or the group is large enough for the central limit theorem to apply. Strong skew or outliers in small groups make the p-value unreliable.
The groups do not need equal variances.
limitations: A p-value above the chosen significance level does not show the groups are equal; it means this data did not provide clear evidence of a difference.
The confidence interval for the mean difference relies on the same assumptions as the test.

mean_difference_ci.calculation: Welch-Satterthwaite interval: (mean of first group - mean of second group) +/- t(0.975, df) x sqrt(s1^2/n1 + s2^2/n2), using the test's degrees of freedom.

response.note: Each row is treated as an independent observation. Paired or repeated measurements of the same subject are not supported.

analysis_question.text: Does the mean of 'score' differ across the two 'group' groups?

box_plot.whisker_rule: Tukey: whiskers reach the most extreme values within 1.5 x IQR of the quartiles.
box_plot.outliers: Values beyond the whiskers are counted in outlier_count.
